_about: What-to-do steps for every AutoPi warning and ML anomaly. Data, not code: edit here. Warnings match on ALL 'match' phrases (first match wins). Anomalies match on the culprit sensor name prefix.

steps: Ease off the throttle now - less load stops the knock.
Next fill-up, use the octane your owner's manual lists; if knock repeats, try a tank of 91+.
If it knocks at normal throttle: check spark plugs and for heat soak (hot day, stop-and-go).
Pull over where it is safe. Turn the heater to full HOT, fan on high.
Idle 1-2 min; if the temp keeps climbing, shut the engine off.
Do NOT open the radiator cap hot. When cool, check the coolant overflow tank.
Look for drips under the car and check the cooling fan runs when hot.
Ease off: lower speed and load, heater to HOT.
If it keeps rising toward 113C, pull over and let it cool.
When cool: check coolant level and clear bugs/debris from the radiator front.
Lean = the ECU is ADDING fuel to make up for extra air.
Listen at idle for a hiss: vacuum leak (PCV hose, intake boots, brake booster line).
Check the intake pipe after the MAF for cracks or loose clamps.
Clean the MAF sensor (MAF cleaner spray only, never touch the wire).
Lean only at high load = weak fuel pump or clogged filter.
Rich = the ECU is PULLING fuel out.
Check the air filter - a clogged filter is the easy fix.
Smell for raw fuel: leaking injector or high fuel pressure.
Clean the MAF sensor - a dirty MAF can over-read.
Short-term trim swinging = live mixture correction.
If it only happens at idle, suspect a vacuum leak.
If it happens everywhere, the front A/F sensor may be slow - watch for a P0130-P0135 code.
Pause 2-3 min at idle when safe - lets the engine and CVT cool.
Use X-Mode / low ratio on climbs and keep a steady, low speed.
If coolant reaches 106C, stop and let it cool.
Idle 30-60 s at light load before turning the car off.
Never shut off right after a hard pull - oil carries heat out of the turbo.

coolant: Coolant is behaving unlike your car's normal.
Watch the temp gauge; when cool, check the coolant level.
Make sure the radiator fan runs when the engine is hot.
stft: Fuel mixture correction is unusual for this situation.
Listen for a vacuum hiss at idle; check intake clamps; clean the MAF.
ltft: Long-term fuel correction moved away from your normal.
Listen for a vacuum hiss at idle; check intake clamps; clean the MAF.
afr: Air/fuel ratio is unusual for this situation.
If it repeats: clean the MAF and check for intake/exhaust leaks.
timing: Ignition timing is unusual - the ECU may be pulling timing.
Check fuel quality (octane) and avoid heavy load until it clears.
rpm: RPM is unusual for this situation (idle surge or hunting).
Check for vacuum leaks and a dirty throttle body; note any CEL.
engine_load: Engine load is unusual for this speed/RPM.
Check the air filter and intake for leaks; dragging brake can also cause it.
boost: Airflow (MAF) is unusual for this situation.
Check the air filter, intake boots and clean the MAF sensor.
intake_temp: Intake air is hotter/colder than normal - heat soak in traffic is common.
If it stays high while moving, check the intercooler for debris.
throttle: Your pedal use is unusual vs your normal - usually just driving style, not a fault.
speed: Speed pattern is unusual vs your normal - usually just the route, not a fault.
_default: Unusual vs your car's learned normal - not a confirmed fault.
If the same sensor keeps getting flagged, follow that sensor's steps.

look._about: Which LIVE GRAPHS page shows the evidence for each warning / ML sensor family. Page names must match graph_pages.
